title: Residential Lease Agreements 2026: Contents, Notarization, Termination
desc: Residential leases under the Housing Law 2023: what to include, notarization, unilateral termination, 30 days' notice, and the right to keep renting.
summary: What a residential lease must contain, notarization, and the cases of termination and unilateral termination under the Housing Law 2023.
body: p

Letting or renting a house is a common transaction, but many contracts are written sketchily and prone to dispute when the landlord wants the house back or the tenant wants to leave early. This article summarizes the rules of the Housing Law 2023 and the Civil Code 2015 on residential lease contracts.
h2
1. What must a residential lease contain?
p
A housing contract must be made in writing and contain the following main terms (Article 163 of the Housing Law):
ol
Full names and addresses of the parties.
A description of the house for lease and the land plot attached to it.
The rent (if the State sets a price, that price applies).
The term and method of rent payment.
The time of handover, and the lease term.
The rights and obligations of the parties; undertakings; other agreements.
The effective date; the date of signing; the parties' signatures (for an organization, a seal if it has one and the signatory's title).
p
The two parties agree for themselves the lease term and rent, and whether rent is paid periodically or in a lump sum. The tenant may only sublease when the landlord agrees (Article 170).
h2
2. Must a lease be notarized?
p

Not mandatory. Under Clause 2, Article 164 of the Housing Law, contracts for leasing, lending, staying in, or authorizing management of a house do not have to be notarized or certified, unless the parties wish to. The effective date is for the parties to agree; if they do not agree, it takes effect on signing.
p

Even so, notarization helps authenticate the signatures and content if there is a dispute. Notarization is done at a notary practice organization; certification at the commune-level People's Committee where the house is located (Clause 4, Article 164). See also Notarizing real estate sale contracts 2026.
h2
3. When does a lease end?
p
For a house that is not public property, under Clause 2, Article 171 the contract ends when:
ul
The lease term expires; if the contract does not state a term, it ends 90 days after the landlord gives notice.
The two parties agree to end it; the leased house no longer exists.
The tenant is an individual who dies or goes missing with no one living with them; the tenant is an organization that is dissolved or goes bankrupt.

The house is seriously damaged or at risk of collapse, lies in an area subject to a land recovery or demolition decision, or is subject to compulsory purchase or requisition: the landlord must give at least 30 days' notice, except in force majeure.
h2
4. Unilateral termination: who may, and when?
p
During the lease term, the landlord may not take the house back on its own, except in the cases in Clause 2, Article 172:
ul
The tenant fails to pay full rent for 3 months or more without an agreed reason.
Uses the house for the wrong purpose; breaks, extends, renovates, or demolishes the house without permission.
Changes the use, lends, or subleases without consent.
Disturbs order or hygiene and has been given a violation record up to a third time without remedying it.
The landlord renovates the house (with the tenant's consent) when 1/3 or less of the lease term remains and the parties cannot agree on a new rent; in this case the landlord must pay compensation.
p

The tenant may unilaterally terminate when the landlord fails to repair serious damage, raises the rent unreasonably or raises it without the notice agreed, or the right to use the house is restricted because of a third party's interests (Clause 3, Article 172).
p
The party terminating unilaterally must give at least 30 days' notice in writing or in the agreed form; a breach that causes damage requires compensation (Clause 4, Article 172).
h2
5. If the house is sold or the landlord dies: is the tenant evicted?
ul

If the owner sells or gives away a house that is let: the tenant may continue renting until the term ends, and the new owner must continue to perform the contract, unless the parties agree otherwise (Article 173).
If the landlord dies: the heirs continue to perform the contract.
If the tenant dies: the person living with them may continue renting until the term ends.
When returning the house, the tenant must return it in the condition in which it was received, apart from natural wear and tear (Article 482 of the Civil Code).
note

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace legal documents. The Housing Law 2023 is partially no longer in force; social housing and public-property housing have their own rules. Income from renting out a house must be declared and taxed under tax law.
